1	# Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	URL: https://radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024
     6	
     7	The Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review provides a comprehensive view of Internet patterns and trends observed through Cloudflare's global network during 2024. The report covers traffic growth, popular services, technology adoption, connectivity disruptions, security threats, and email security trends. Data is derived from Cloudflare's position as a provider protecting and accelerating websites and applications for millions of customers worldwide.
     8	
     9	## Internet Traffic Growth and Popular Services
    10	
    11	Global Internet traffic grew by 17% in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. The trend line starts mid-January to normalize for post-holiday activity.
    12	
    13	Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.
    14	
    15	| Rank | Service   |
    16	|------|-----------|
    17	| #1   | Google    |
    18	| #2   | Facebook  |
    19	| #3   | Apple     |
    20	| #4   | TikTok    |
    21	| #5   | AWS       |
    22	| #6   | Microsoft |
    23	| #7   | Instagram |
    24	| #8   | YouTube   |
    25	| #9   | Amazon    |
    26	| #10  | WhatsApp  |
    27	
    28	![Top 10 most popular Internet services worldwide](./assets/top-10-internet-services.jpg)
    29	
    30	SpaceX Starlink traffic saw dramatic 3.3x growth during 2024, continuing to bring satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. Starlink is not yet available globally; the trend line is scaled relative to peak observed request volume.
    31	
    32	![Normalized Starlink traffic worldwide showing 3.3x growth in 2024](./assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Technology Adoption and Usage Patterns
    35	
    36	Several key adoption metrics emerged from the 2024 data:
    37	
    38	- **Mobile OS**: 33% of traffic came from iOS devices. Apple iOS and Google Android remain the dominant mobile operating systems, with peak Android traffic share exceeding 95% in some regions and peak iOS reaching around 66%.
    39	- **HTTP/3**: 21% of traffic uses HTTP/3, the most recent version of the protocol that runs on top of QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.
    40	- **Search Engines**: Google dominates with 89% of search engine referral traffic, followed by Yandex (3.1%), Baidu (2.7%), Bing (2.6%), DuckDuckGo (0.95%), and other engines (2.2%).
    41	- **Browsers**: Chrome remains the most popular browser globally.
    42	- **API Client Languages**: Go is the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, followed by Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%), and .NET (3.6%).
    43	
    44	Post-quantum encryption saw a dramatic surge in adoption during 2024. Starting at around 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17, rapidly climbing to approximately 12-13%. Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing.
    45	
    46	![Post-quantum encrypted traffic worldwide showing rapid adoption after Chrome 124 release](./assets/post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg)
    47	
    48	## Internet Connectivity and Disruptions
    49	
    50	Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. These outages result from a variety of causes, and the Cloudflare Radar Outage Center tracks their scope and duration using Cloudflare traffic data.
    51	
    52	The leading causes of Internet disruptions were:
    53	
    54	| Cause                | Count |
    55	|----------------------|-------|
    56	| Government Directed  | 116+  |
    57	| Cable Cut            | 41    |
    58	| Unknown              | 16    |
    59	| Power Outage         | 16    |
    60	| Technical Problem    | 9     |
    61	| Military Action      | 9     |
    62	| Weather              | 8     |
    63	| Maintenance          | 4     |
    64	| Cyber Attack         | 4     |
    65	| Natural Disaster     | 1     |
    66	| Fire                 | 1     |
    67	
    68	![Causes of major Internet disruptions observed in 2024](./assets/internet-disruption-causes.jpg)
    69	
    70	IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic during 2024. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.
    71	
    72	41% of global traffic came from mobile devices, reflecting the continued importance of mobile connectivity worldwide.
    73	
    74	## Security Landscape
    75	
    76	Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed, indicating the scale of ongoing threats. The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries.
    77	
    78	The Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later, underscoring the persistent nature of widely known vulnerabilities.
    79	
    80	RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) valid routes increased by 6.4%, an important step toward improved Internet routing security.
    81	
    82	## Email Security Threats
    83	
    84	Cloudflare's email security analysis revealed that 4.3% of emails processed were malicious. Among those malicious emails, 43% contained a deceptive link designed to trick recipients. The top-level domain .bar originated the largest share of malicious and spam email observed during the year.
    85	
    86	## Key Findings
    87	
    88	- Global Internet traffic grew 17% year-over-year, with Starlink traffic surging 3.3x as satellite connectivity expanded to underserved regions.
    89	- Post-quantum encryption adoption leapt from approximately 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic following Chrome 124's default enablement in April 2024.
    90	- Government-directed shutdowns remained the leading cause of the 225 major Internet disruptions observed, followed by cable cuts (41 incidents) and power outages (16).
    91	- Security threats remained pervasive: 6.5% of all traffic was mitigated, Gambling/Games was the most targeted sector, and Log4j exploitation persists years after disclosure.
    92	- Go surpassed other languages to become the most popular API client language, capturing roughly 12% of automated API traffic.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Constants
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)
ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_PATH = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# Cloudflare Radar dark/navy palette
BG_COLOR = RgbColor(0x0A, 0x0E, 0x1A)       # Very dark navy
ACCENT_ORANGE = RgbColor(0xF6, 0x81, 0x1F)  # Cloudflare orange
TEXT_WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
TEXT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xB0, 0xB8, 0xC8)
TEXT_LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0x8A, 0x94, 0xA6)
CARD_BG = RgbColor(0x11, 0x18, 0x27)

def set_slide_bg(slide, color=BG_COLOR):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size, bold=False, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf

def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size, color=TEXT_GRAY, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.level = 0
    return tf

def add_line(slide, left, top, width, color=ACCENT_ORANGE, thickness=Pt(3)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, thickness)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def add_card(slide, left, top, width, height, color=CARD_BG):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    # Remove rounded corners by setting adj value (optional, keep subtle)
    return shape

# Create presentation
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

# ==========================================
# Slide 1: Title
# ==========================================
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide1)

# Accent bar at top
add_line(slide1, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, ACCENT_ORANGE, Pt(4))

# Title
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(1.5),
            "Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review",
            Pt(48), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Subtitle
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(3.6), Inches(11.333), Inches(1),
            "A data-driven analysis of global Internet traffic, adoption trends, connectivity disruptions, and security threats",
            Pt(20), bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Footer line
add_line(slide1, Inches(4), Inches(4.6), Inches(5.333), TEXT_LIGHT_GRAY, Pt(1))

# Audience tag
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(5.0), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.6),
            "Technology Executives & Network Infrastructure Leaders",
            Pt(14), bold=False, color=TEXT_LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ==========================================
# Slide 2: 17% Global Traffic Growth and Starlink's 3.3x Surge
# ==========================================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide2)

add_line(slide2, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, ACCENT_ORANGE, Pt(3))
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.8),
            "17% Global Traffic Growth and Starlink's 3.3x Surge",
            Pt(32), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Left card: 17% growth
add_card(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.3), Inches(5.8), Inches(2.4), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.5), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.7),
            "+17%", Pt(48), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.7), Inches(2.2), Inches(5.4), Inches(1.2),
            "Year-over-year growth in global Internet traffic, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation.",
            Pt(14), color=TEXT_GRAY)

# Right card: Starlink 3.3x
add_card(slide2, Inches(6.8), Inches(1.3), Inches(5.8), Inches(2.4), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(7.0), Inches(1.5), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.7),
            "3.3x", Pt(48), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(7.0), Inches(2.2), Inches(5.4), Inches(1.2),
            "SpaceX Starlink traffic surge during 2024, bringing satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. Trend normalized relative to peak observed request volume.",
            Pt(14), color=TEXT_GRAY)

# Image bottom center
img_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg")
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide2.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(3.0), Inches(4.0), width=Inches(7.333))

# ==========================================
# Slide 3: Google Leads Top 10 Services as Generative AI Rises
# ==========================================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide3)

add_line(slide3, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, ACCENT_ORANGE, Pt(3))
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.8),
            "Google Leads Top 10 Services as Generative AI Rises",
            Pt(32), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Left: table of top 10
add_card(slide3, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.5), Inches(5.5), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.35), Inches(5.1), Inches(0.4),
            "Top 10 Most Popular Internet Services", Pt(16), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

services = [
    ("#1", "Google"), ("#2", "Facebook"), ("#3", "Apple"), ("#4", "TikTok"), ("#5", "AWS"),
    ("#6", "Microsoft"), ("#7", "Instagram"), ("#8", "YouTube"), ("#9", "Amazon"), ("#10", "WhatsApp")
]

y = 1.85
for rank, svc in services:
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.9), Inches(y), Inches(0.8), Inches(0.35), rank, Pt(13), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(1.6), Inches(y), Inches(3.8), Inches(0.35), svc, Pt(13), color=TEXT_WHITE)
    y += 0.42

# Right: image + AI insight
img_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "top-10-internet-services.jpg")
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide3.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(6.5), Inches(1.2), width=Inches(6.0))

add_card(slide3, Inches(6.5), Inches(4.6), Inches(6.0), Inches(2.1), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(6.7), Inches(4.75), Inches(5.6), Inches(0.4),
            "Generative AI on the Rise", Pt(16), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(6.7), Inches(5.2), Inches(5.6), Inches(1.3),
            "Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. Rankings based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

# ==========================================
# Slide 4: Post-Quantum Encryption Jumps from 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3
# ==========================================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide4)

add_line(slide4, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, ACCENT_ORANGE, Pt(3))
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.8),
            "Post-Quantum Encryption Jumps from 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3",
            Pt(32), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Left: PQE image
img_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg")
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide4.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), width=Inches(6.2))

# Right: stats cards
add_card(slide4, Inches(7.0), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.8), Inches(1.6), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(7.2), Inches(1.35), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.5),
            "2% → 13%", Pt(36), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(7.2), Inches(1.95), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.7),
            "Post-quantum encryption share of TLS 1.3 traffic after Chrome 124 enabled it by default on April 17, 2024. Firefox and Safari have also begun rollout.",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

add_card(slide4, Inches(7.0), Inches(3.1), Inches(5.8), Inches(1.3), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(7.2), Inches(3.25), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
            "HTTP/3: 21% Adoption", Pt(22), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(7.2), Inches(3.75), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.5),
            "The latest protocol version running on QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

add_card(slide4, Inches(7.0), Inches(4.6), Inches(5.8), Inches(2.0), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(7.2), Inches(4.75), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
            "Go Becomes Top API Client Language", Pt(22), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(7.2), Inches(5.25), Inches(5.4), Inches(1.1),
            "Go leads with ~12% of automated API requests, followed by Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%), and .NET (3.6%).",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

# ==========================================
# Slide 5: 225 Major Disruptions: Government Shutdowns Lead Outage Causes
# ==========================================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide5)

add_line(slide5, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, ACCENT_ORANGE, Pt(3))
add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.8),
            "225 Major Disruptions: Government Shutdowns Lead Outage Causes",
            Pt(32), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Left: image
img_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "internet-disruption-causes.jpg")
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide5.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), width=Inches(6.0))

# Right: table
add_card(slide5, Inches(7.0), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.5), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide5, Inches(7.2), Inches(1.35), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
            "Causes of Major Internet Disruptions (2024)", Pt(16), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

causes = [
    ("Government Directed", "116+"),
    ("Cable Cut", "41"),
    ("Unknown", "16"),
    ("Power Outage", "16"),
    ("Technical Problem", "9"),
    ("Military Action", "9"),
    ("Weather", "8"),
    ("Maintenance", "4"),
    ("Cyber Attack", "4"),
    ("Natural Disaster", "1"),
    ("Fire", "1"),
]

y = 1.85
for cause, count in causes:
    add_textbox(slide5, Inches(7.2), Inches(y), Inches(3.8), Inches(0.3), cause, Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)
    add_textbox(slide5, Inches(11.0), Inches(y), Inches(1.6), Inches(0.3), count, Pt(13), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    y += 0.42

# ==========================================
# Slide 6: 6.5% of Traffic Mitigated: Persistent Threats and Bot Concentration
# ==========================================
slide6 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide6)

add_line(slide6, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, ACCENT_ORANGE, Pt(3))
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.8),
            "6.5% of Traffic Mitigated: Persistent Threats and Bot Concentration",
            Pt(32), bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Top row: 3 cards
add_card(slide6, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(3.9), Inches(2.2), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.35), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.6),
            "6.5%", Pt(40), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.7), Inches(2.0), Inches(3.5), Inches(1.2),
            "of all traffic processed by Cloudflare was mitigated, indicating the massive scale of ongoing threats.",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

add_card(slide6, Inches(4.7), Inches(1.2), Inches(3.9), Inches(2.2), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(4.9), Inches(1.35), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.6),
            "Gambling & Games", Pt(22), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(4.9), Inches(1.95), Inches(3.5), Inches(1.2),
            "The most attacked industry category observed across Cloudflare's global network in 2024.",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

add_card(slide6, Inches(8.9), Inches(1.2), Inches(3.9), Inches(2.2), CARD_BG)
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(9.1), Inches(1.35), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.6),
            "68%", Pt(40), bold=True, color=ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(9.1), Inches(2.0), Inches(3.5), Inches(1.2),
            "of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries, showing extreme geographic concentration.",
            Pt(13), color=TEXT_GRAY)

# Bottom row: 2 cards
add_card(slide6, Inches(0.5), Inches(3.7), Inches(6.0), Inches(2.8), CARD_BG)
